problems.location: Concept 1: Sociocultural and Neurological Foundations of Learning / block 1
problems.lesson_text: "Learning is an active verb; it is something people do, not something that happens to them. Through acting in the world, people encounter situations, problems, and ideas... and they adapt."
problems.source_text: “Learn” is an active verb; it is something people do, not something that happens to them. People are not passive recipients of learning, even if they are not always aware that the learning process is happening. Instead, through acting in the world, people encounter situations, problems, and ideas.
problems.reason: The quote changes “Learn” to “Learning” and silently drops a whole sentence and the word “Instead,” without marking the cut.

problems.location: Concept 2: Cognitive Processes and Evidence-Based Learning Strategies / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Generating causal explanations significantly outperforms rote memorization of complex texts (Pressley et al., 1987).
problems.source_text: in an early study, people were asked either to provide “why” explanations for several unrelated sentences or to read and study the sentences. Both groups were then tested on their memory of the sentences. Those who asked questions performed better than the group that just studied the sentences (Pressley et al., 1987).
problems.reason: Pressley et al. (1987) tested memory for unrelated sentences, not complex texts; the source credits the complex-material finding to other researchers (McDaniel and Donnelly, 1996).

problems.location: Concept 5: Evaluating Learning Technologies: Affordances, Multimedia Design, and Universal Design / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Reading identical on-screen text aloud verbatim, overloading the visual phonological loop.
problems.source_text: Redundancy Principle. People learn better from graphics and narration than from the combination of graphics, narration, and on-screen text.
problems.reason: The phonological loop is the sound-based, verbal part of working memory, so a "visual phonological loop" does not exist; redundant on-screen text loads the visual channel.

problems.location: Concept 5: Evaluating Learning Technologies: Affordances, Multimedia Design, and Universal Design / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Minimizes non-relevant mental fatigue and accidental penalty, keeping cognitive capacity reserved for learning.
problems.source_text: Low physical effort. The design can be used efficiently, comfortably, and with a minimum of fatigue.
problems.reason: The source's principle is about low physical effort (its example is large buttons for students with limited fine motor skills), but the lesson recasts it as cutting mental fatigue to save cognitive capacity.

problems.location: Exercise 4.1: Categorizing educational AI tools along the continuum from visible conversational agents to ambient sorting systems / block 4
problems.lesson_text: Recommendation is visible, sorting is invisible
problems.source_text: Decides what shows up next. Nothing announces itself here. Things just arrive in an order chosen for you.
problems.reason: The answer key calls the recommendation engine visible, but the source puts choosing what shows up next on the hidden side, as does the lesson's own Concept 4 list ("Choosing: Content recommendation engines" under INVISIBLE AI).

problems.location: Concept 4: The Spectrum of Visible and Invisible Artificial Intelligence in Learning / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Destroys psychological safety; induces evaluation anxiety, exacerbates stereotype threat, and criminalizes normative behaviors
problems.source_text: It can give peace of mind on one side of the screen. On the other side, it’s a record.
problems.reason: The source presents watching AI as two-sided and says none of the nine types is good or bad on its own, while the lesson states flatly that it destroys psychological safety and criminalizes normal behavior.

problems.location: Concept 4: The Spectrum of Visible and Invisible Artificial Intelligence in Learning / block 3
problems.lesson_text: Because subsequent educators encounter the diagnostic label before the person, institutional expectations drop, reifying initial deficits into permanent structural ceilings.
problems.source_text: It can feel like being understood. It also means next year’s teacher meets the label before they meet the learner.
problems.reason: The source gives sorting both a benefit and a cost and asks how a learner gets out of a group, while the lesson asserts that sorting locks deficits into permanent ceilings.

problems.location: Concept 2: Cognitive Processes and Evidence-Based Learning Strategies / block 2
problems.lesson_text: Alternate diverse problem types in assignments instead of grouping problems by single topic.
problems.source_text: Researchers have identified potential benefits of variable and interleaved practice learning, but they have also found a few benefits for blocked practice.
problems.reason: The source says interleaving helps most with highly similar categories while blocking helps with dissimilar ones, but the lesson tells leaders to interleave everywhere with no caveat.

problems.location: Concept 2: Cognitive Processes and Evidence-Based Learning Strategies / block 4
problems.lesson_text: Rereading text, highlighting handouts, or watching a clean presentation creates a subjective feeling of fluency that learners mistake for mastery.
problems.source_text: not in source
problems.reason: No source discusses an "illusion of competence" from highlighting or watching presentations; How People Learn II only notes that immediate massed re-reading does not promote learning.

problems.location: Concept 4: The Spectrum of Visible and Invisible Artificial Intelligence in Learning / block 3

problems.reason: No source says automated scorers favor dominant cultural dialects or routinely screen out culturally diverse work; Compass only says one rubric for everybody leaves little room for what makes a person interesting.

problems.location: Concept 4: The Spectrum of Visible and Invisible Artificial Intelligence in Learning / block 3
